brief: Monthly Goldman Sachs Prime Services positioning report; it reports hedge fund data for September 2026 without arguing a thesis. Global Fundamental L/S funds returned -0.55% asset-weighted (vs MSCI TR -1.19%, YTD +12.6%), with +0.73% alpha driven by short side gains outweighing long losses; Info Tech, momentum and asset selection were the largest alpha contributors. Systematic L/S returned +3.46%, the best month YTD, driven entirely by short side alpha. Global equities were modestly net sold as short sales outpaced long buys and gross trading activity rose at its fastest pace in four months. Overall Prime Book gross leverage rose 3.3 points to 309.7% (68th percentile) while net leverage fell to 77.6%; US Fundamental L/S net leverage hit a one-year low of 45.7%. Regionally, North America was net sold for the first time in five months, Europe saw its largest net buying in over five years, and EM Asia was heavily sold. By US sector, TMT (Info Tech, Comm Svcs) was the only sector bought; Consumer Discretionary, Energy, Health Care and other cyclicals/defensives were net sold, with Energy seeing its largest selling in nearly three years.
